work: Quaestiones evangelicae ad Stephanum, Quaestio IV: Julius Africanus' letter to Aristides on the genealogies (Greek excerpt, quoted by Eusebius)
author: Eusebius of Caesarea (quoting Julius Africanus)
date: Africanus c. 220-240 AD; Eusebius's quotation c. 320-340 AD (approx., not checked)
ref: PG 22, Quaestio IV (Africanus excerpt, note 12 at cols 899-900); sentence at cols 901-902, note (14)
original: Ματθὰν ὁ ἀπὸ Σολομῶνος, ἐγέννησε τὸν Ἰακώβ· Ματθὰν ἀποθανόντος, Μελχὶ ὁ ἀπὸ Νάθαν ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς γυναικὸς ἐγέννησε τὸν Ἡλί· ὁμομήτριοι ἄρα ἀδελφοί, Ἡλὶ καὶ Ἰακώβ· Ἡλὶ ἀτέκνου ἀποθανόντος, ὁ Ἰακὼβ ἀνέστησεν αὐτῷ σπέρμα, γεννήσας τὸν Ἰωσὴφ, κατὰ φύσιν μὲν ἑαυτῷ, κατὰ νόμον δὲ τῷ Ἡλί· οὕτως ἀμφοτέρων υἱὸς Ἰωσήφ
original_edition: Migne, Patrologia Graeca 22, cols 901-902. Read from archive.org OCR (patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_022_djvu.txt) and the page image (PDF p. 480 rendered and viewed). OCR text, accents not checked letter by letter against the printed page.
english: Own translation: Matthan, of Solomon's line, begot Jacob. After Matthan died, Melchi, of Nathan's line, begot Heli by the same woman; so Jacob and Heli were uterine brothers. When Heli died childless, Jacob raised up seed to him, begetting Joseph, who was by nature his own son but by law Heli's son; thus Joseph was the son of both.
translator: own translation (no English text of Ad Stephanum read)
page: PG 22 cols 901-902 (printed column headers 901/902 seen on PDF p. 480)
edition: J.-P. Migne, Patrologia Graeca vol. 22; archive.org Google scan, OCR
what_it_says: Eusebius, quoting Africanus, gives the levirate solution: Matthan and Melchi married the same woman, Jacob and Heli were half-brothers, and Joseph was Jacob's son by nature and Heli's by law. The passage names no daughter and no Mary-line.
limits: Africanus' letter survives only inside Eusebius. Greek is OCR. The sentence does not mention Mary at all; the 'son of both' wording is about Joseph.

work: Quaestiones evangelicae ad Stephanum, Quaestio III (gamma paragraph)
author: Eusebius of Caesarea
original: Ματθαῖος μὲν γὰρ ὁμολογουμένως τὴν ἔνσαρκον γένεσιν ἱστορῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀποδεῖξαι βουλόμενος ἀληθὲς ἐκ Δαβὶδ, ὅθεν ἐχρῆν τῇ εἰσβολῇ κέχρῆσθαι τοῦ λόγου· τὸν δὲ Λουκᾶν ἡγοῦμαι μὴ τὴν κατὰ σάρκα γένεσιν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ γενεαλογεῖν ἐθέλοντα
original_edition: Migne PG 22, cols 895-896. OCR text (archive.org djvu) checked against page image PDF p. 477; the word 'κέχρῆσθαι' restored from OCR 'χέλρηται' and is uncertain.
english: Own translation: Matthew, faithfully recounting the fleshly birth of Christ and wishing to show that Joseph was truly from David (which is where the account had to begin); but I think Luke did not intend to trace the fleshly birth of Jesus in his genealogy.
what_it_says: Eusebius says Matthew traces Christ's fleshly birth through David to Joseph, while in his view Luke does not intend to trace the fleshly descent at all (his own second solution, about the sonship given at baptism).
use: answer to objection (Eusebius's alternative: Luke's list is not the fleshly line)
limits: Eusebius does not say Luke gives Mary's line; the Greek is OCR and the translation is my own.

work: Church History, Book I, ch. 7 (Africanus' levirate solution, as quoted by Eusebius)
author: Eusebius of Caesarea (quoting Julius Africanus)
ref: Eusebius, HE I.7.5, I.7.9-10, I.7.17 (NPNF2 numbering of sections)
original_edition: not read (Greek of HE I.7 not checked)
english: 17. Thus far Africanus. And the lineage of Joseph being thus traced, Mary also is virtually shown to be of the same tribe with him, since, according to the law of Moses, intermarriages between different tribes were not permitted. For the command is to marry one of the same family and lineage, so that the inheritance may not pass from tribe to tribe.
translator: Arthur Cushman McGiffert (NPNF2 vol. 1, as printed on New Advent)
page: page unknown (New Advent HTML, Book I, chapter 7)
edition: Schaff & Wace eds., NPNF2 vol. 1, via newadvent.org
what_it_says: Eusebius passes on Africanus's levirate explanation; he then says that Mary is 'virtually shown' to belong to the same tribe as Joseph, but names no father for Mary and does not say Luke gives her line.
use: supports (the earliest surviving source for the levirate solution; Mary's tribe only)
limits: The levirate account explains Joseph's two fathers without Mary. 'Same tribe' is weaker than a Davidic line claim.

work: Expositio Evangelii secundum Lucam, Book III (section 15)
author: Ambrose of Milan
date: c. 377-390 AD (approx.; date per patristic database in search result)
ref: Expositio in Lucam III.15 (Luke 3:23-24; Matthew 1:16 comparison)
original: Lucas vero [Joseph], cui desponsata erat Maria, filium Heli; Heli autem filium Melchi esse descripserit (Luc. 3, 24).
original_edition: Migne PL 15, approx. cols 1318-1319 (column markers in the OCR). Read from archive.org OCR (patrologiaecur15mign_djvu.txt). Bracketed word restored from OCR fragments; not character-verified. Critical text: CSEL 32/4 (Schenkl), not read.
english: Own translation: But Luke has Joseph, to whom Mary was betrothed, [as] son of Heli, and Heli [as] son of Melchi.
page: PL 15, Expositio III.15, approx. cols 1318-1319 (OCR column markers)
what_it_says: Ambrose calls Joseph, the betrothed of Mary, son of Heli, and explains the two fathers by the levirate account taken from Eusebius (HE I.7). He does not say Heli was Mary's father.
use: context (closest pre-1500 wording to 'Heli as Joseph's father-in-law' is only 'to whom Mary was betrothed')
limits: OCR; the sentence is about Joseph's paternity; no statement that Luke gives Mary's line. Ambrose cites Eusebius HE I.7 for the levirate explanation.

work: De consensu evangelistarum, Book II, ch. IV, sec. 11 (Harmony of the Gospels)
author: Augustine of Hippo
ref: De consensu evangelistarum II.4.11 (numbering as on the BKV/NPNF1-06 page)
original: Lucas vero, quia non proprie dicitur genitus, qui vel adoptione efficitur filius, vel in successione mortui ex illa quam uxor ejus fuit nascitur, non dixit: Heli genuit Joseph; aut, Joseph quem genuit Heli: sed qui fuit, inquit, filius Heli; sive adoptando, sive a propinquo genitus in mortui successione nascendo.
original_edition: Latin from archive.org OCR (patrologiaecurs09goog_djvu.txt, Migne volume identity unclear, not PL 9 as first assumed). OCR garbled in places ('nuii di\it' read as 'non dixit'); not verified against print.
english: And the evangelist has shown clearly enough that he did not name Joseph the son of Heli on the ground that he was begotten of him, but only on the ground that he was adopted by him.
translator: not confirmed on the fetched page (NPNF1-06 text, Schaff ed.)
page: page unknown (NPNF1-06 Book II ch. IV sec. 11)
edition: NPNF1 vol. 6 (Schaff ed., 1888) text as hosted by Bibliothek der Kirchenvater (bkv.unifr.ch)
what_it_says: Augustine says Luke calls Joseph 'son of Heli' by adoption, not by begetting; Heli is Joseph's adoptive father, not Mary's.
limits: Augustine does not identify Mary's father at this point; the Latin is OCR. The brief's claim that Augustine later abandoned this view was not checked (Retractations not read).

work: Contra Faustum Manichaeum, Book XXIII, ch. 4
author: Augustine of Hippo
ref: Contra Faustum XXIII.4 (CAPUT IV of Book XXIII)
original: Nos ergo credimus etiam Mariam fuisse in cognatione David, quia Scripturis eis credimus, quae utrumque dicunt, et Christum ex semine David secundum carnem (Rom. 1,3, et II Tim. 2,8), et ejus matrem Mariam, non cum viro concumbendo, sed virginem (Matth. 1,18, et Luc. 1,27).
original_edition: Migne PL 42, Contra Faustum XXIII.4. Read from archive.org OCR (patrologiaecursu0042mign_djvu.txt); the book/chapter heading read from OCR. Column not reliably read. CSEL 25 (Zycha) not read.
english: Own translation: We therefore believe that Mary also was of David's kin, since we believe the Scriptures, which say both that Christ was of David's seed according to the flesh and that his mother Mary was a virgin who had not known a man.
page: PL 42, Contra Faustum XXIII.4 (column not read)
what_it_says: Augustine asserts Mary's Davidic kinship from Scripture. He rejects Faustus's claim that Mary's father was Joachim of the tribe of Levi, and calls the apocryphal book that names Joachim as Mary's father of no canonical authority.
use: supports (pre-1500 Mary Davidic); objection answer (Joachim as Mary's father is rejected)
limits: Augustine does not say Luke's genealogy is Mary's. The Latin is OCR; the Joachim argument rests on the apocryphal book, which he refuses to treat as authoritative.

work: An Exposition of the Orthodox Faith, Book IV, ch. 14 (Concerning our Lord's genealogy and the holy Mother of God)
author: John of Damascus
original_edition: Greek not read (Migne PG 94 not located on archive.org in a usable form)
english: Born then of the line of Nathan, the son of David, Levi begot Melchi and Panther: Panther begot Barpanther, so called. This Barpanther begot Joachim: Joachim begot the holy Mother of God. And of the line of Solomon, the son of David, Mathan had a wife of whom he begot Jacob. ... Joseph, therefore, is by nature the son of Jacob, of the line of Solomon, but by law he is the son of Heli of the line of Nathan. ... But that Joseph is descended from the tribe of David is expressly demonstrated by Matthew and Luke, the most holy evangelists. But Matthew derives Joseph from David through Solomon, while Luke does so through Nathan; while over the holy Virgin's origin both pass in silence.
translator: E. W. Watson and L. Pullan (NPNF2 vol. 9, as printed on New Advent)
page: page unknown (New Advent Book IV, ch. 14)
edition: Schaff & Wace eds., NPNF2 vol. 9, via newadvent.org
what_it_says: Damascene gives a separate Davidic line for Mary (Nathan, Levi, Melchi, Panther, Barpanther, Joachim), while saying Matthew and Luke trace Joseph and pass over Mary's origin. He does not say Luke's list is Mary's.
use: supports (pre-1500 Mary Davidic descent via a separate list); also shows the 'Mary's line' idea existed before 1500 but not as a reading of Luke
limits: Damascene's Mary-list is not Luke's list. Greek not read. English read verbatim.

work: Summa Theologiae III, q. 31, a. 3, reply to objection 2
author: Thomas Aquinas
original_edition: Latin not read (corpusthomisticum.org returned an error)
english: Although Damascene (De Fide Orth. iv) says that the Blessed Virgin Mary was connected with Joseph in as far as Heli was accounted as his father, for he says that she was descended from Melchi: yet must we also believe that she was in some way descended from Solomon through those patriarchs enumerated by Matthew ... and all the more since Ambrose states that Christ was of the seed of Jechonias.
translator: English Dominican Province translation as hosted on CCEL (credit line not read)
edition: CCEL online text of the Summa
what_it_says: Aquinas reports Damascene's view that Mary is connected with Joseph because Heli was 'accounted as his father', and that Mary was descended from Melchi. He does not say Luke gives Mary's line. He also gives the QVNT answer that Heli and Joseph were differently descended from David.
use: context (a pre-1500 scholastic reading of Damascene; still no explicit Luke=Mary claim)
limits: Aquinas's paraphrase of Damascene is not Damascene's text. Latin not read.

work: In Lucae Evangelium Expositio, Book II (comment on Luke 3:23)
author: Bede
ref: In Lucam II, on Luke 3:23 (Qui fuit Heli ...)
original: Deinde ex una tribu fuisse Joseph et Mariam, unde et lege eam accipere cogebatur, ut propinquam. Et quod simul censentur in Bethlehem, ut de una videlicet stirpe generati, atque ideo per generationem Joseph, origo quoque Mariae monstretur.
original_edition: Migne PL 92, In Lucae Evangelium Expositio lib. II. OCR from archive.org (patrologiaecursu0092mign_djvu.txt), obvious OCR errors corrected ('Deiude' -> 'Deinde', 'Mari:' -> 'Mariae'); not checked letter by letter against print.
english: Own translation: Next, Joseph and Mary were from one tribe, so that the law also made him take her as a close relative; and because they were registered together at Bethlehem, as born of one stock, therefore through Joseph's genealogy the origin of Mary is also shown.
page: PL 92, In Lucam II (column not read)
what_it_says: Bede argues that because Joseph and Mary shared one tribe and one stock, Luke's genealogy through Joseph also shows Mary's origin; he takes the levirate solution from Africanus via Eusebius.
use: supports (nearest pre-1500 approach to 'Luke shows Mary's line'); not an explicit claim that Heli is her father
limits: Bede's sentence is an inference from shared stock, not a statement that Luke's list is Mary's. OCR.

author: anonymous
english: And the priest remembered the child Mary, that she was of the family of David, and undefiled before God.
translator: Alexander Walker (ANF vol. 8 edition; credit not printed on the fetched page, from search snippet, unverified)
edition: Roberts & Donaldson eds., Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 8, via tertullian.org
what_it_says: The text says Mary is of David's family (2nd-century source). Joachim is named as her father in the same work, but the text does not say Heli.
use: supports (earliest Mary-Davidic statement in this set)
limits: Protevangelium never equates Joachim with Heli; it does not talk about Luke. Greek not read.

author: Jerome
english: At the request of Hedibia, a lady of Gaul much interested in the study of scripture, Jerome deals with the following twelve questions. ... (3) How are the discrepancies in the evangelical narratives to be accounted for? How can Matt. xxviii. 1 be reconciled with Mark 16:1, 2.
translator: NPNF2 (New Advent page; translator not read)
what_it_says: Ep. 120 is a list of resurrection and harmony questions; none concerns the genealogies, Mary's line or Heli. The text (questions 1-9 fetched; 10-12 searched by keyword) mentions no genealogy.
use: objection (negative: Jerome's 'harmony' letter does not contain the Luke=Mary view)
limits: Only the English text was read; keyword search (genealog, Heli, Mary) found nothing.

work: Elucidations (ANF vol. 6), note on Julius Africanus, Elucidation I (note 9)
author: ANF editors (Roberts & Donaldson, editorial note)
date: 19th-century ANF editorial note (exact year not read)
ref: ANF6, Africanus Elucidation I, paragraphs 1-4 (note 9 is at para. 3)
english: The opinion that Luke's genealogy is that of Mary was unknown to Christian antiquity. In the fifteenth century it was first propounded by Latin divines to do honour (as they supposed) to the Blessed Virgin. It was first broached by Annius of Viterbo, a.d. 1502.
translator: editorial note in ANF6 (translator of Africanus excerpt not relevant)
page: ANF6 p. 127 (note header: 'Joseph the son of both, p. 127')
edition: Roberts & Donaldson eds., Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 6, via tertullian.org
what_it_says: A 19th-century editorial note says the Luke=Mary view was unknown to antiquity, first proposed by Latin divines in the 15th century, and first broached by Annius of Viterbo in 1502.
use: objection (a secondary claim about 'first proponents'; needs checking, not a source)
limits: The note cites no sources. It conflicts with the 1498 date in the brief, and its 'antiquity agreed' claim omits Damascene's separate Mary-list and Bede's 'origo Mariae' remark, which are close to the Mary-line view.

work: Antiquitatum variarum volumina XVII (Index/Tabula entries on Pseudo-Philo commentary)
author: Annius of Viterbo (Giovanni Nanni)
date: first edition 1498 (per brief; not seen); copy read is the 1515 reprint
ref: Tabula of the Antiquitates, Philonis commentary, book IV (index entries, not body)
original: Qz differt fi fcribas Helylivel Elt, Qzeadéfunc;Helyh:Helyachím & loachím
original_edition: archive.org item bib_fict_1023716 (Antiquitatum variarum volumina XVII, 1515), OCR of the index lines; body text not located. OCR garbled.
english: Own translation of index line: 'Whether one should write Heli or Eli makes a difference; ... Heli, Eliachim and Joachim.'
edition: Antiquitatum variarum volumina XVII (1515), archive.org scan
what_it_says: The index of this 1515 reprint lists 'Heli or Eli' and 'Heli, Eliachim and Joachim' under the commentary on Pseudo-Philo; the index says four objections to the genealogy are answered. The body text was not found, so Annius's actual claim (Heli = Joachim? Mary's father?) is not verified.
use: objection (Annius's claim is still UNVERIFIED in body text)
limits: Index only; no body text found in OCR; the 1498 edition was not read. Index wording is not a claim that Luke gives Mary's line.

work: Commentarius in Matthaeum (ch. 1, on the genealogy)
author: Hilary of Poitiers (attribution in question)
original_edition: not located in a usable edition
what_it_says: Not located. Web search returned only secondary Catena Aurea / Golden Chain quotations attributed to Hilary's Quaestiones (unverified).
limits: Earlier I mistook archive.org item patrologiaecurs09goog for Hilary; it is Augustine's De consensu evangelistarum (see item G2-05). Hilary's Matthew commentary remains UNVERIFIED.

work: Quaestiones Veteris et Novi Testamenti (cited by Aquinas as 'Qq. Vet. et Nov. Test.')
author: pseudonymous (ascribed in the Middle Ages to Augustine and to Hilary; not settled)
ref: cited by Aquinas, ST III q31 a3 ad 2 (part i qu. lvi; part 2 qu. vi)
what_it_says: Aquinas reports this work's answer: Luke does not say Joseph was Heli's son in begetting; Heli and Joseph were differently descended from David. The primary text was not read.
use: answer to objection (reported via Aquinas only)
limits: Known only from Aquinas's citation; the attribution and wording are UNVERIFIED.

author: Gregory of Nazianzus
original_edition: Migne PG 36 (archive.org gr_vol_036 OCR); keyword search for Heli / genealogy; no statement found
what_it_says: Negative in OCR: no passage found in PG 36 that says Heli is Mary's father or that Luke gives Mary's line. A web summary claimed Or. 38 says this; not confirmed.
use: objection (negative result; claim not supported in OCR)
limits: Keyword OCR search only; the Orations are not read in full.

author: Epiphanius of Salamis
original_edition: archive.org gr_vol_042 OCR searched for Ἰωακείμ and Ἄννα: no hit (OCR poor)
what_it_says: Negative in OCR: Greek 'Joachim' not found in the PG 42 text tried. The claim that Epiphanius says Heli was Mary's father is UNVERIFIED.
limits: OCR search only; PG 42 identity of the Panarion section not confirmed; Williams translation not read.

author: J. Gresham Machen
ref: chapter on the genealogies (p. 206 per a secondary quotation)
what_it_says: Secondary web sources say Machen takes Luke's list as Joseph's ancestry (Heli Joseph's father), not Mary's. Not read in primary text.
limits: Only secondary sources (Desiring God, Modern Reformation search snippets). No primary text read.

work: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke (Luke 3:23)
author: F. Godet
what_it_says: Secondary sources (Coffman, Church of God commentary) say Godet took Luke's list as Mary's line. Primary text not read.
limits: Only secondary summaries; the claim is UNVERIFIED.
